issues.explanation: down() re-adds the old unique(queue_id, code) index while tickets from different days may legitimately share a code, so after the feature has been used a rollback fails with a duplicate-key error and no data handling is provided; the migration is therefore not truly reversible in practice.

The uniqueness check only adds defaults for levels 0/10/20 that are not explicit keys, so custom entries on other levels can still collide with the range fallback: {"10":"X","15":"P"} is accepted although priority 1 (default P) and 15 (custom P) share the P sequence, and {"0":"X","5":"N"} is accepted although priority <=0 (default N) and 5 (custom N) collide.

The factory test hardcodes issued_at 2026-09-28 and expects N001 for it, but the preceding ticket is created at the real 'today'; on 2026-09-28 both share the same issue_date and the old ticket would get N002, making this test fail that day.

prefixOwner() is declared as a global function inside a Pest test file, which pollutes the global namespace and risks a redeclaration error if the file is loaded twice; a closure or a namespaced helper would be safer.

review.summary: The change implements priority-derived ticket codes with daily per-prefix restarts end to end: queue defaults and a validated custom map, per-day/per-prefix nextCode, single-clock issuance, factory support, the two schema migrations and the required documentation, backed by a broad new Pest suite. The main gaps are a down() that cannot be rolled back once cross-day duplicate codes exist and a uniqueness hole for custom keys outside 0/10/20, plus a date-dependent test; none of these break the normal path, so the PR is approvable with minor follow-ups.
